# [TASK] actor-service: expose crew credits (director/producer) for filmography filtering

## Task
Expose crew credits (director/producer/etc.) in actor-service, alongside the
existing cast-only filmography.

## Scope
DTO + service method, plus a REST endpoint — #203 runs in ai-service, a
separate microservice, so a Java-only method would be uncallable from it;
exposing it over HTTP is what "which will call whatever this Task exposes"
(below) actually requires. Not in scope: the natural-language parsing or
the cross-service aggregation call itself (that's #203).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `TmdbPersonMovieCreditsResponse` gains a `crew` field (`List<TmdbCrewCredit>`) alongside the existing `cast`, mapped from TMDB's real `person_movie_credits` response (`job`, `department` included)
- [x] `ActorService` exposes a method to fetch a person's crew credits filterable by department/job (e.g. Directing/Director, Production/Producer), following the same shape as the existing cast-based filmography path — plus `GET /api/v1/actors/{id}/crew?department=&job=`, so #203 can actually reach it over HTTP
- [x] Existing cast-only behavior and endpoints are unchanged — additive only, verified at the HTTP layer (same fixture hit via both `/movies` and `/crew`, not just by inspection)
- [x] Unit + WireMock integration tests cover a person with both cast and crew credits, and a person with crew-only credits

## Estimate
**Hours:** 5

## Notes
Surfaced by ADR-020 during #201's review: actor-service had no data path for `role=DIRECTED`/`PRODUCED`.

Added `TmdbCrewCredit` (exact ADR-020 shape), `CrewCreditDto`, `ActorMapper` crew mappings, `ActorService.getCrewCredits(id, department, job)` (case-insensitive, unpaginated — mirrors `getFilmography`), and the controller endpoint. ARCHITECTURE.md's actor-service endpoint list updated.

The crew-sort test fixtures were rewritten so release-date order runs opposite to alphabetical job order — the original fixtures let a "sorts by job instead of date" bug pass unnoticed.
